title: Choosing a System Display Language

children:
You can define which language that you want the system to display text 
 for the system, RF, Insight Screens, and Trading Partner Management windows. This setting 
 is made at the network user level. The system uses the language setting in the 
 Windows Control Panel to govern in what language the system displays text. 
 This is helpful if you have different users whom require different language 
 configurations. For instance, when you change the Windows language setting 
 during a Remote Desktop Services client session, you can log onto SCALE using 
 any machine, and the language setting will "travel" with you. You can perform this action on the Windows Control Panel (Regional and 
 Language Options) Window or the Web User Window.

NOTE: In this topic, the term "user profile" refers to the Windows 
 network user that an employee is signed onto via Remote Desktop Services. This 
 does not refer to a SCALE user 
 profile.
The following is discussed in this topic:
Choosing a Display Language for SCALE Application Windows and RF Screens
Choosing a Display Language for Web Screens
Choosing a Display Language for Insight Screens
Choosing a Display Language for History and Server-Side Processing

Choosing a Display Language 
 For SCALE Application Windows and RF Screens...

When you implement a language 
 change, all SCALE windows will display this new language in field names, 
 window titles, system-supplied records, error messages, and any other 
 text that the system generates. See the SDK topic "Choosing a Display Language For RF Screens" for more details.

Access the Windows 
 Control Panel (Start | Control 
 Panel).

Access the Regional 
 and Language Options screen.

On the Regional 
 Options Tab, select a language and press OK.

IMPORTANT: For your changes to take effect, you need to exit 
 and restart the system/RF module. The system will use the new language to display 
 windows when accessed only by the user whose profile you are changing 
 with this procedure. All other users will see the language that is defined 
 on      their Windows' profile records.

You will need to perform 
 the following step to complete the implementation of a new language on your RF devices. The system will reference a setting on your web browser to display the correct language on the RF.

Open the Internet 
 Explorer web browser.

Go to the option Tools | Internet 
 Options, and press the Languages Button.

Press the Add 
 Button, choose the language you would like to add, and press OK. 
 The system will add your new selection to the "language preference" 
 list.

Move your new 
 language to be the first in the "language preference" list, 
 and press OK. The system will save your changes, and the RF device will 
 now display this new language.

Choosing a Display Language 
 for Web Screens...

When you implement this 
 language change, all web screens will display this new language in field 
 names, window titles, error messages, and any other text that the system 
 generates. However, the main log on page will always use the application 
 server's language, regardless of a specific web user's language preference.

Open the Configurations 
 Explorer, and access the Web User Window.

Open the web 
 user profile record that you want to select a language for, and 
 select the General Tab.

Use the Language 
 Selection Field to indicate which language you want the system 
 to use when displaying text on the web windows.

Press OK. 
 The system will save the record.

IMPORTANT: For your changes to take effect, you need to exit 
 and restart the Internet Explorer browser. The system will use the new 
 language to display windows when accessed only by the user whose profile 
 you are changing with this procedure. All other users will see the language 
 that is defined on      their profile 
 records.
Choosing a Display Language for Insight Screens...

When you implement a language change, all Insight screens will display this new language in field names, window titles, error messages, and any other text that the system generates. This can be achieved by changing the browser language setting, or by changing the operating system’s language and region settings. These settings vary, depending on device type and operating system version.

With the Insight screens, multiple browsers and devices are supported.  It should be noted, however, that certain languages/regions are not necessarily implemented on all supported browsers. Additionally, if there are fields on the web screens that are not translated, some may still display in the application server’s language.

Changing the language selection on a desktop browser (e.g., Internet Explorer) usually includes the localization formatting for date-time and decimal separators.  For example, if the languages of "Spanish (Mexico)" and "Spanish (Spain)" are listed, they each have different corresponding locale settings. However, on many tablets and mobile devices (e.g., iPad), there is a region setting which is separate from the language setting. Please consult your manufacturer’s device manual or specific browser for detailed information on how to properly set the language region.
Choosing a Display Language For History and Server-Side Processing...
Additionally, if you want history and server-side processing to be reflected in a different language, you will need to make these additional changes:
Select the desired language (for the ILSSRV user) in the Windows Regional and Language Options.
Change the "Default System Language" in the SCALE Technical Values Window to the desired language.

Since the client machine installer runs before the Database Environment selection, the system will retrieve error messages during the client machine install from the "Default" database configured in the

file (based on the Windows user's culture).  The "Default" database may not contain the same language translations as the other database environments.
